title: feat(storage): the upload-link page names the record and field for the link's own user
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoSLDKWQ8v7cxY9uDGijfncD)_

Fixes #32712

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：上传链接页面（智能体用 `create_upload_link` 发给用户的那个页面）现在对链接本人多显示两行：「记录　报销单「出租车 11-12」」和「放入　「发票」字段」（附件链接显示「附件」；记录还没创建时显示「一条新的报销单（尚未创建）」）。到期时间改成按用户自己的时区显示；过了时间，页面直接说「已过期，请索取新链接」并禁用发送。
- **为什么改**：裁决 B′。用户同时打开几个链接时，以前每个页面一字不差，传错单、或者智能体绑错单，页面上都看不出来；单文件字段还会直接覆盖原文件。
- **风险与回滚**：名字是在页面打开时以链接本人的身份读出来的，走的是他自己读记录的同一条路，所以只显示他在应用里本来就能看到的内容；标题被屏蔽、不可读，或者标题字段不是文字类（比如指向另一条记录的查找字段，它的值是一串编号）时只显示对象名；字段不可读时那一行不显示；读不到就退回到原来的页面。他已经无法读取这条记录、或者已经不在这个组织里时，得到的是和陌生人一样的 404。上传成功后页面不会再被「已过期」盖掉。上传接口的拒绝逻辑一个字没改。回滚就是还原这个 PR。
- **先看**：`record-file-access.ts` 的 `namesForLinkUser`（以谁的身份读、什么情况下返回 404、什么情况下少显示），再看 `upload-link-page.ts` 的 `targetRows` 和脚本里的到期判断。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-storage exec vitest run src/record-file-access.integration.test.ts -t "ruling B′"`，预期 14 个用例全部通过。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。

## What changes

<details><summary>The names, read as the link's own user (ruling B′, record 6842088322)</summary>

- `inspectUploadLink(token, callerUserId, options?)` takes `options.names = { lang }`. Only the page `GET` asks for it; the `PUT` door's inspect is unchanged.
- The names are read only after `openLink` has found the link open, unexpired and the caller's. A stranger, an expired, a used or an unknown link never reaches the read and keeps today's one 404.
- `namesForLinkUser` resolves the link's user with the same `resolveUserContext` the upload uses. It then reads the record with `engine.findOne(object, { where: { id } }, { context: user })`, the caller read `read_file` already does. ⛔ There is no system read.
  - The read answers no row, or refuses `403` / `404`: the existing unusable-link 404 page.
  - The user can no longer act in the link's organization (`resolveUserContext` answers `null`): the same 404 page.
  - Any other failure: the page names nothing, as on `main`, with one `warn`.
- **Title.** The object's display field (`resolveDisplayField`, ADR-0079), as that read serves it. It is shown only when the security service answers it queryable for that user (`getQueryableFields`: readable and not masked). It is never `id`, never blank, and never equal to the record's id. Round 2: the column must also be title-typed (`isTitleEligible`, or the autonumber primary) and declare no `maskingRule`, the gate `engine-reference-name-visible.ts` applies to the engine's own title disclosure. `resolveDisplayField` honours an explicit `nameField` on any type, and a lookup, master_detail, user or select display field serves a foreign id or a machine value. Such a record then shows the object's label only.
- **Field label.** Shown only when the field is in `getReadableFields` for that user.
- **Fail closed.** A security service without one of those methods, or one that answers `undefined`, shows less. With no security service, no field-level rule exists, and the served row is the answer.
- **Labels.** The object's and the field's own labels, in the page's language. They go through `translateObject` over the i18n service's bundle, the same glue the analytics label pass builds. A missing label is left out and ⛔ never replaced by an API name.
- **A link for a record not yet created** has no record to read. It shows the object's label as "a new …, not created yet" and the field row.

</details>

<details><summary>The page</summary>

- Two rows in a `<dl>`: `Record` / `Goes into`. They degrade in steps: label + title, then label only, then no rows (today's page). The names are HTML text only. ⛔ They are not in the script's data, not in an attribute, and not in the tab title, which stays `copy.pageTitle`.
- The header comment's #30892 "names no record, field, user or organization" is rewritten to cite B′.
- **Expiry (i).** The server still prints the UTC-named text, now inside a `<time id="expires" datetime="ISO">`. The script rewrites it in the reader's own time zone, in the page's language. A browser running no script keeps the UTC text.
- **Expiry (ii).** The script takes the server's `now` and keeps the difference from the browser's clock. Once the printed expiry has passed, it shows the expired line and disables the picker and Send. It does so at load, before a pick, before a send, and on a timer while the page stays open. Round 2: pressing Send stops the timer, and from then on the line belongs to the send. A send still running at the moment is not talked over, and a file that landed is never followed by "expired". A send that fails re-arms the timer while the link has time left. The server's one unusable-link refusal is unchanged.
- `upload-link-copy.ts`: eight new entries in all 11 languages (`recordRow`, `goesIntoRow`, `recordTitled`, `recordOfObject`, `recordNotYetCreated`, `intoField`, `intoAttachments`, `expired`). The refusals still name nothing, and its header comment says why.

</details>

<details><summary>Wiring (claim amendment 6867825002)</summary>

- `storage-routes.ts`: the page route passes `{ names: { lang: copy.lang } }`.
- `storage-service-plugin.ts`: `bindRecordFileAccess` binds `getI18n`, which reads the `i18n` service per call.
- `file-attachment-service.ts` is pass-through only. It hands the options argument on, widens the `getSecurity` type by the two read methods, and adds `getI18n` to its `recordFiles` pick.

</details>

What a page reads like now, rendered from this branch (`upload-link-page.ts` with fixed views):

```text
[en] record link:        Record | Expense "Taxi 11-12"          | Goes into | the "Receipt" field
[en] title masked:       Record | Expense                       | Goes into | the "Receipt" field
[en] attachments link:   Record | Expense "Taxi 11-12"          | Goes into | Attachments
[en] not yet created:    Record | a new Expense line, not created yet | Goes into | the "E-invoice" field
[zh-CN] record link:     记录 | Expense「Taxi 11-12」 | 放入 | 「Receipt」字段
[zh-CN] not yet created: 记录 | 一条新的Claim（尚未创建） | 放入 | 「Invoices」字段
nothing readable:        today's page, no rows
```

## Tests

<details><summary>New pins (record-file-access.integration.test.ts, describe "#32712 (b) — ruling B′", 14 cases)</summary>

- The owner sees both rows in English and in Chinese. No id, API name, user or organization appears anywhere in the page, the tab title is generic, and the script's data carries no name.
- Labels come through an `i18n` service stood in for the case (`报销单` / `保单` in zh-CN); English without an entry falls back to the declared labels.
- An attachments link, a multi-file field, and records not yet created (`count` 1 on a single-file field, `count` 3 on a multi-file field) each show their rows.
- A masked title, a hidden title, and a security service that cannot say what is masked all show the object's label only. The title's words appear in no byte of the HTML or the headers.
- A field the owner cannot read loses its row.
- A record the owner can no longer read gets the 404 page byte-identical to a stranger's and to an unknown token's, nonce aside, in English and in Chinese.
- Round 2, the other two 404 paths. A user whose membership is gone (`resolveUserContext` answers `null`) gets the stranger's 404 byte for byte, and the page names the record again once the membership is back. A record read the engine refuses `403` or `404` gets the same 404; a `500` gives today's page with no rows.
- Round 2, a lookup as `nameField` (`trip.claim_ref`). The read serves the bare claim id, and the page in English and Chinese shows `Record | Trip` only. Neither id nor the claim's title is in the HTML or the headers.
- Opening the page three times leaves the `sys_file` count, the link row and the record unchanged, and the link then takes its upload. The claim is scoped to those rows: on an object opted into read audit, the name read is a detail read as the user, so each open may enqueue one `read` ledger row, an honest record of a view.
- CONTROL: another user, the reviewer who reads every claim, an expired link and a used link all get the one refusal, byte-identical to `main`'s unusable page.
- The expiry is rewritten in the reader's time zone (the script run on a stubbed DOM).
- The client-side expired state: expired on the server's clock with the browser behind (disabled at once, nothing fetched); live on the server's clock with the browser ahead (it sends); and the timer flipping an open page.
- Round 2, the send owns the line. Send clears the timer. After the attached answer, firing that timer anyway and a later pick leave "attached". A send still running at the moment keeps "Uploading…", then shows "attached". A failed send re-arms the timer, and the moment then shows "expired".
- Changed: the existing zh-CN page test reads the expiry inside the `<time>` element. `upload-link-copy.test.ts` calls the new entries and holds each language to carrying them.

</details>

<details><summary>Ablations: each negative pin, with the forbidden behaviour put back (17, all red, all restored)</summary>

Every mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, with the anchor hit 1→0 and the blob changed. The suite imports `src`, so no build leg is involved. Each restore was proven with blob == HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty. Logs: `server-seat-7/r2026-11-13/out/32712b-evidence/ablations*.log`.

| # | Put back | Red |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | the record read as the system | 404 byte-for-byte |
| A2 | an unreadable record degrades instead of answering 404 | 404 byte-for-byte |
| A3 | no masked check on the title | masked title |
| A4 | a security service without `getQueryableFields` fails open | masked title (its third leg) |
| A5 | no readability check on the field | unreadable field |
| A6 | the tab title names the record | owner rows (generic title) |
| A7 | the names ride the script's data | owner rows (script data) |
| A8 | no client-side expiry | expired state |
| A9 | the browser's clock alone (`skew=0`) | expired state |
| A10 | no local-time rewrite | local expiry |
| A11 | the object label untranslated | i18n labels |
| B1 | no title-type gate (round 2) | lookup `nameField` |
| B2 | a user no longer in the organization degrades | left the organization |
| B3 | a `403` / `404` read refusal degrades | read refused |
| B4 | the expiry writes over a send | the send owns the line |
| B5 | Send does not stop the timer | the send owns the line (cleared) |
| B6 | a failed send is not re-armed | the send owns the line (failed leg) |

The first attempts at A3 and A5 were refused by the tool itself: the replacement text was a substring of the anchor, so its count did not rise. They were rerun with a distinct replacement and went red. Neither first attempt ran a test. In round 2, A3 and A5 were run again at the new head, and both were still red (`ablations-r2.log`).

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **Item (a) holds on `main` 5e250a65.** Measured by rendering `main`'s page sources: en and zh-CN copy, with the expiry written as "November 13, 2026 at 03:05 AM UTC" / "2026年11月13日 UTC 03:05". The eval (6842586067, 03:06Z) saw English and an RFC-1123 GMT string, which is the pre-#32891 page. #32891 merged at 01:43Z the same day. **Inference, not a measurement:** the deployed build predated #32891. The deployed sha is not readable from here.
- **No record yet (#32686 links).** These show the object's label and the field only. There is no record to read, the user held the object's create permission at mint, and the field row still asks field readability as that user.
- **No object label.** When the object declares no label, the record row is dropped, never shown as an API name. Not pinned: the fixture objects all declare labels.
- **A declared `maskingRule` on the title column.** It drops the title, as the engine's title gate does. This leg is not pinned. With a security service, the masked case is pinned through `getQueryableFields`; without one, nothing masks the user's own read.
- **Clock.** The expiry check runs on the server's clock as sent with the page, so a browser whose clock is off neither disables a live link nor sends into a dead one. Network latency makes it err permissive by that latency, never stricter than the server.
- **Clause-② (widening).** The page shows more to its own user. One `GET` now answers the unusable 404 where `main` served 200: an owner who can no longer read the record, or is no longer in the organization. B′ mandates this, and the `PUT` already refused both cases, so no working path is removed. The `PUT` door, its codes, statuses and the one unusable-link answer are byte-unchanged.
- `UPLOAD_LINK_TTL_SECONDS` (10 minutes) is untouched. Eval 6842606859 measured two agent-minted links expiring before the user reached them, so whether to lengthen it or make it configurable is left to the card's owner.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-mcp-record-files.dogfood.test.ts:548` still says the pre-record page "names nothing". Its assertions (no API name, no email) still hold, and the file is outside this card's surface.
